title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is seeing a mix of new ventures and ongoing challenges, particularly in satellite technology and international security. As companies jockey for position, the health of existing infrastructure, like the ISS, remains a concern.

themes.title: New Ventures in Satellites
themes.body: Starlink veterans are launching a startup aimed at expanding megaconstellation ownership, indicating a shift towards more competitive satellite landscapes. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's recent $190M Series C funding reflects growing investor interest in space-based capabilities.

themes.title: ISS Health Concerns
themes.body: Recent repair spacewalks on the ISS underscore ongoing worries about the station's long-term viability. As the aging platform continues to face technical challenges, the debate over its future intensifies.

themes.title: Defense Spending on the Rise
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup has added $1.4B to the space resilience line, highlighting an increasing recognition of space as a critical domain for national security. This influx of funding may bolster various defense initiatives, including satellite development.

themes.title: International Security in Orbit
themes.body: Europe's next security challenge is emerging in the orbital arena, reflecting the geopolitical complexities of space. As nations recognize the strategic importance of space assets, collaboration and competition are expected to escalate.
